title: Vx and Vy vs Density Altitude
conditions: Gross weight 3600 lb, landing gear retracted, full throttle and max RPM, wing flaps retracted, mixture adjusted for smooth operation, cowl flaps open

verification.method: Multi-engine: both curves re-measured at 6 independent pixel-calibrated altitudes (SL, then every ~1500-4000 ft up to 15000 ft); both fit remarkably linear trends (slope consistent to within ~3% across all sampled points) with NO crossing within the charted range -- the two lines converge but Vx stays below Vy throughout, contrary to the original model's implied crossing around 9000 ft. Single-engine: the chart draws Vx and Vy as a single 'tent' shape that visually converges to ONE point at the single-engine ceiling (confirmed by locating the apex pixel directly) -- the original model's separate, unequal atCeiling values for vx/vy did not reflect this.
verification.changeFromOriginal: Multi-engine vy.seaLevel corrected 105->112 (7%), vy.at15000 corrected 90->99 (10%), vx.at15000 corrected 100->94 (6%). Single-engine values were all more significantly off: vx.seaLevel 84->94 (12%), vy.seaLevel 96->105 (9%), and critically, atCeiling was modeled as two different values (vx=80, vy=85) when the chart actually shows both converging to the SAME value (measured 98) at the ceiling -- a structural error, not just a magnitude error. ceilingDa 7000->7189 (3%, within normal reading tolerance); note this is close to but not identical to the independently re-measured 3600 lb single-engine ceiling on fig5-10 (6925 ft) -- a ~260 ft (4%) cross-chart discrepancy that may reflect normal POH drafting tolerance between the two source figures.
verification.confidence: High for multi-engine (6-point fits, very linear). High for single-engine SL and ceiling-convergence finding; the exact ceilingDa/atCeiling pixel read has the usual single-point reading uncertainty (+/- 1-2%).
